newsitem.title: USA: Miss. official announces $3.36 billion tobacco deal. [CORRECTED 23:49 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Miss. official announces $3.36 billion tobacco deal. [CORRECTED 23:49 GMT]

text.p: Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore announced a $3.36 billion (corrects from $3.6 billion) settlement with the tobacco companies Thursday and called on Congress and the White House to approve a $368.5 billion national accord.
Moore told a news conference that the agreement would reach the $3.36 billion (corrects) mark in 25 years but said payments would continue "forever."

Moore made the announcement less than a week before the state was scheduled to become the first to go to trial with cigarette makers to recoup tax money spent treating Medicaid recipients for smoking-related illnesses. The Mississippi lawsuit had sought about $940 million in damages overall.

The state's settlement would be eclipsed by the national accord, which was reached last month by the industry and attorneys general for 40 states, but which requires approval from Congress. The larger agreement has stirred criticism among tobacco opponents and in Congress.
"I'm pleading for the president and the Congress to pass this bill," Moore told reporters at the Mississippi state capitol.
"All the things that will help our children will have to be passed by the national Congress. We've provided the leverage so that Congress can now act," he said.
